disclaimer: Not legal advice. This watches trip-wires we set ourselves. When one trips the answer is always to talk to somebody who does this for a living — the point is that the conversation happens BEFORE the thing it was about.

tripped.obligation: Confirm that depicting Pokémon card imagery, set names and product photography in a commercial product is defensible.
tripped.why: Universal community practice, card images sourced from the standard community API with attribution. No revenue yet.
tripped.trigger: ANY of: the first dollar of revenue · a paid tier · sponsorship or ads · a cease-and-desist of any kind · media coverage large enough to be noticed.
tripped.note: This is the one that ends the company rather than costing it money. Everything else on this list is a bill.
firedBy: revenue machinery appeared in the code

tripped.obligation: Resolve whether displaying PokemonPriceTracker-derived prices publicly is permitted on our tier.
tripped.why: Free tool, no revenue, development phase. Their terms reserve commercial use for the $99 tier and describe lower tiers as personal and development use.
tripped.trigger: The first dollar. Also: any claim on our surfaces that the data is commercially licensed.
tripped.note: The realistic downside is being cut off, not sued — which is an operational risk, and worst at launch.
firedBy: revenue machinery exists while PPT figures are published

watching.trigger: ANY of: the first draw with a non-Tyler participant · any prize over $500 · any entry method that could be read as consideration · operating across a border.
ANY of: spending money on the name (merch, print, paid ads) · incorporating under it · a trademark application · significant public traction under it.
ANY of: a login · a stored email beyond the newsletter · anything tied to a Discord identity · analytics that identifies an individual.
